episode_title: Maximizing Profits Through Smarter Pricing with Brian Doyle of Holden Advisors

real_qa.q: What is pricing power and how do B2B companies measure it according to Holden Advisors?
real_qa.r: Pricing power is determined first by evaluating the value you provide to customers—whether through increasing revenue, reducing expenses, or minimizing risk. Then you assess that value in context of the market, competition, and how customers utilize it. After determining the value independently, you evaluate how much of it you can actually capture through your go-to-market motion and sales strategy, which might be 40–50% depending on whether your salespeople believe in and can articulate that value against sophisticated buyers.

real_qa.q: How can B2B companies discover customer willingness to pay without asking directly?
real_qa.r: Instead of asking customers directly about willingness to pay, engage them in discovery conversations about how they use your product or service, what value they derive, what the alternative looks like, and what would happen if they weren't using it. Customers are very open to sharing this information. A third-party consultant asking these questions often gets even more candid responses than the company's own sales team, because customers may hesitate to criticize the sales rep directly to company leadership.
real_qa.requete: customer value discovery B2B pricing research

real_qa.q: What is the quarry company's express line strategy and how did it create competitive differentiation?
real_qa.r: A quarry company (number three in their market) discovered that customers were waiting 45 minutes in line for dirt delivery, costing them thousands per hour in truck and driver idle time at construction sites. By creating an express line that reduced wait time from 45 minutes to 5 minutes, the company essentially created a TSA PreCheck service for dump trucks. This differentiation, based on quantified customer pain, moved them to number one in the market.
real_qa.requete: quarry TSA PreCheck dump truck express line pricing

real_qa.q: What are the four categories of B2B buyers according to Holden Advisors?
real_qa.r: There are four buyer categories: price buyers (only 1.5% of the market) who care only about lower price; value buyers who understand the math and buy on value; relationship buyers who want hand-holding and ease; and poker players, who are relationship or value buyers pretending to be price buyers—typically procurement or sourcing professionals who deploy negotiation playbooks to extract concessions.
real_qa.requete: four types B2B buyers procurement categories

real_qa.q: What is the gift-gets negotiation tactic and how does it expose whether a buyer is truly price-focused?
real_qa.r: When a buyer demands lower price, offer to reduce the price by removing value elements—for example, replacing a dedicated account manager with pool support. If they are a true price buyer, they will accept. If they are a poker player playing hardball, they will object and reveal that those value elements actually matter to them, shifting the conversation from price to value. This exposes their real priorities and gives you leverage to defend your pricing.
real_qa.requete: gift-gets negotiation tactic procurement discount strategy

real_qa.q: Why should B2B sales professionals view negotiations with procurement as a game?
real_qa.r: When you understand that negotiation with procurement is a game with predictable tactics—ghosting, waiting until quarter-end, emotional manipulation—you gain comfort and patience. Procurement professionals are using taught playbooks to do their job; recognizing this prevents you from getting emotionally wound up and making poor decisions like dropping your price unnecessarily. Staying calm and patient leads to better outcomes and more civil interactions.

guest.bio_context: Brian Doyle started his career as an Air Force pilot flying missions around the world. He then transitioned to the commercial space, working as a Six Sigma Master Black Belt at General Electric, followed by roles in sales and marketing at GE and smaller companies. Seven years ago, he joined Holden Advisors after discovering their expertise in pricing strategy and negotiation. He eventually became CEO as the founder stepped away and his leadership team took over the business.
